{% comment %} The full sample list is in the DOM -- every sample, which on a large project is thousands of rows -- and DataTables only cuts it to one page once it initialises. Rendering that raw table first makes the page briefly enormous and then snaps it shut, dragging everything below it back up the screen. The wrapper holds the height a paged table will occupy and keeps the rows out of layout until they are paged. {% endcomment %}

{% if metadata_summary.available %} {% comment %} On-demand sample-metadata summary. The payload is aggregate counts only -- never per-sample rows -- so it stays a few hundred bytes regardless of project size, and is computed in project_page() from the runs dict that is already in memory. That is why it is embedded rather than fetched: a lazy endpoint would cost a second full project document read from MongoDB per click, which is the expensive part on a 2,000-sample project. Nothing renders until the button is pressed; Plotly is already loaded above for the classification figures. {% endcomment %} {{ metadata_summary|json_script:"metadata-summary-data" }}

{% comment %} Click-through from a cancer type to that type's samples within this project. POSTed rather than linked: /search_results/ accepts POST only, and keeping it that way means no new crawlable URL that runs a search per request. The GET route is not an alternative -- gene_search_page reads project_name but never filters on it, so a GET link would show results from every project under a heading naming this one. No classquery inputs on purpose. search_results reads "no boxes checked" as no_filter, which returns every sample including the no-amp ones -- the right default for "show me all the X samples here". {% endcomment %}
